leads.name: Elm '260' (rare DED-resistance clone)
leads.reason: One of only 20 known specimens in the world per Brighton & Hove Museums, part of the National Elm Collection. Not pursued to publication because it reads as scientifically rare rather than genuinely old or visually spectacular (a disease-resistance test clone, not a veteran tree), and no age/size figures were found. Worth a second look if a source ever gives it a story beyond rarity.

leads.name: TROBI champion Ulmus x hollandica 'Wredei' (golden elm)
leads.reason: TROBI-registered champion, measured 2009 at 17m height, 57cm dbh (~179cm girth). Modest size for a champion and no story or age found beyond the register entry; girth suggests a young-to-middle-aged ornamental cultivar rather than an ancient specimen. Parked rather than blocked: worth revisiting with a fresh TROBI pull or a Blakers Park-specific search.
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species

leads.name: Old Steine elms (general)
leads.reason: The brief named Old Steine as a candidate cluster. Multiple sources describe Old Steine's elms collectively ("the Old Steine War Memorial would look very barren if it wasn't for the elms") but no source found names or measures an individual specimen there, which is exactly the 'nobody named it' pattern this project's own research notes flag as low-yield. Worth a targeted revisit (council tree survey, TROBI search by postcode) rather than a generic sweep.

leads.name: Three mature Wych elms, tennis pavilion path, Queen's Park
leads.reason: Friends of Queen's Park describes these as 'probably aged over 100 years old' but does not name or measure them individually, and they are distinct from the champion Wych Elm already shipped as bhm_005. Population description, not a single collectible point; leave for a future pass with a site visit or a named source.

leads.name: Stanmer churchyard yew
leads.location: St Mary's churchyard, Stanmer Park, Brighton
leads.reason: Council Special Trees of Stanmer Park page calls the hollow yew probably Brighton's oldest tree, well over 500 years, girth 5.94 m (ancient class); Ancient Yew Group lists two yews north of the church (last visited 1999). Needs a pin and a look at the beech avenue and cedars, then a story.

leads.name: Stanmer Park Turkey oak (tallest oak in Brighton)
leads.reason: Council Special Trees of Stanmer Park trail no. 10: Quercus cerris, 'more than 30 metres, the tallest oak in Brighton'. No girth, age or coordinate on the fetched page (positions are in the trail app only); no photo or exact pin in reach. A park-level pin would be a 500 ha park, not a small site.
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species

leads.name: Stanmer Park sweet chestnut (30 m) and champion Siberian elm / Chinese ash
leads.reason: Council trail nos. 7, 8, 12: sweet chestnut 30 m high, planted 19th century; Ulmus minor x pumila planted 1965, 'British Isles height and girth champion'; Chinese ash British Isles height champion. Planted champions, not veterans, and no coordinates on the page; needs the council trail app positions or a GPS fix.

leads.name: Stanmer Great Wood beech avenue
leads.reason: Council trail no. 16: avenue of veteran beeches planted about 300 years ago along a carriage drive, storm-damaged in 1987. An avenue is not one collectible point; no individual beech named or measured.

leads.name: Dyke Road Park champion Belgian elm (Ulmus x hollandica 'Belgica')
leads.reason: Wikipedia (Ulmus x hollandica 'Belgica') says TROBI champion at Dyke Road Park, 17 m by 92 cm dbh in 2009 (about 290 cm girth, derived). Single secondary source, 2009 measurement, no coordinate or photo, a cultivar of modest size; alive not confirmed.

leads.name: Preston Park West Ride Jersey elm row
leads.reason: Search summary only (not a fetched page): row of Jersey elms about 29 m tall, about 2 m girth, planted around 1880. A row is not a collectible point; no individual named.

blocked.name: St Nicholas churchyard, Dyke Road
blocked.location: St Nicholas Church, Dyke Road, Brighton
blocked.reason: Church Heritage Record states no ancient, veteran or notable trees are connected to this church; council local-list entry names no tree. Nothing to ship; do not re-search.

blocked.name: Extra-Mural Cemetery yews and oaks (general)
blocked.reason: Sources describe the cemetery's tree population collectively ('the cemetery contains many yew trees along with oaks, beech, rowan, holly') with no individual specimen ever named, dated or measured anywhere found. Fails the collectible-point test: there is no one obvious place to stand. Blocked rather than left as a lead because the brief explicitly named this site and it was checked and came up empty; a future pass should not re-run this exact search without a new angle (e.g. a council tree survey PDF, if one exists, comparable to the Stanmer Park one).

blocked.name: Woodvale Cemetery specimen trees (general)
blocked.reason: Council and heritage sources describe the cemetery's 'many fine specimen trees' in general terms only; no individual tree found named, aged or measured. Same failure mode as the Extra-Mural Cemetery. Blocked for now; a council arboriculture survey, if one exists, would be the way back in.
